questions.prompt: An order event must be published once and delivered to several subscribed applications. Which service is designed for this publish-subscribe pattern?
questions.explanation: SNS topics deliver published messages to subscribed endpoints. This supports fanout to multiple consumers.

questions.prompt: Before launching a workload, a team wants to estimate costs using planned resource sizes and usage. Which tool should it choose?
questions.explanation: Pricing Calculator models expected charges from proposed configurations. An estimate supports planning and is not a guarantee of the final bill.

questions.prompt: A company has several AWS accounts and wants consolidated billing through a centrally managed organization. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: Organizations helps centrally manage AWS accounts and supports consolidated billing. It preserves separate accounts while simplifying administration.

questions.prompt: A stable compute workload can commit to a consistent hourly spend for one or three years. Which pricing model can reduce eligible usage costs?
questions.explanation: Savings Plans exchange a usage-spend commitment for lower eligible rates. They differ from interruptible Spot capacity.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants to automate and centrally manage backup policies across supported AWS services. Which service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: AWS Backup centralizes backup management for supported resources. A backup plan defines the required protection schedule.

questions.prompt: A migration project needs to move database data to AWS while minimizing interruption to the source application. Which service should the team evaluate?
questions.explanation: AWS DMS supports database migration and replication. Keeping the source usable during migration can reduce application downtime.

questions.prompt: Analysts want to run SQL queries against data stored in Amazon S3 without operating a query server. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: Athena provides serverless SQL querying for data in S3. It avoids running and maintaining a dedicated query cluster.

questions.prompt: A media application needs managed image analysis to identify objects in uploaded photographs. Which service is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Rekognition provides image and video analysis. Transcribe handles speech rather than identifying objects in photographs.

questions.prompt: A contact centre wants to turn recorded customer calls into written transcripts. Which service is the best match?
questions.explanation: Transcribe converts speech into text. Image recognition and network configuration services do not perform this task.

questions.prompt: A website needs rules that inspect HTTP requests and block common application-layer attacks. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: WAF filters web requests using configured rules. It addresses application-layer request controls rather than storage or analytics.

questions.prompt: A company is evaluating an AWS service focused on protection against distributed denial-of-service attacks. Which service matches this purpose?
questions.explanation: Shield provides DDoS protection. Compliance reports and storage volumes serve different purposes.

questions.prompt: Administrators want a central way to manage operating-system tasks, including patching supported managed nodes. Which service should they evaluate?
questions.explanation: Systems Manager supports operational management of managed nodes, including patch management. It is suited to fleet administration.

questions.prompt: A security team needs automated vulnerability findings for supported EC2 workloads and container images. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: Inspector assesses supported workloads for vulnerabilities and produces findings. Pricing and DNS tools do not perform vulnerability assessment.

questions.prompt: A company retains records for years, rarely retrieves them and accepts delayed access. Which S3 storage option should it evaluate?
choices: S3 Standard for frequent immediate access
questions.explanation: Glacier Deep Archive is intended for long-term, rarely accessed objects. Retrieval delay and minimum-duration charges need consideration.

questions.prompt: An operations team wants information about AWS events that may affect resources in its own account. Which service should it use?
questions.explanation: AWS Health provides visibility into relevant service events and affected resources. This complements the team's own application monitoring.

questions.prompt: A team regularly removes unused resources and chooses appropriately sized services to reduce unnecessary spending. Which Well-Architected pillar is most directly involved?
questions.explanation: Cost optimization focuses on delivering business value while avoiding unnecessary expense. Resource sizing and eliminating waste directly support it.

questions.prompt: An application needs to retrieve a database password from a managed secret store and support password rotation. Which service best fits?
questions.explanation: Secrets Manager stores and manages secrets and supports rotation. This avoids embedding long-lived passwords directly in application code.

questions.prompt: A cook tastes a sauce with a spoon and needs to taste it again. Which practice prevents contamination?
choices: Use a new clean tasting utensil for the second taste
Dip the same spoon back into the sauce
Wipe the used spoon on an apron
Rinse the used spoon briefly in the sauce
questions.explanation: A used tasting utensil can transfer microorganisms from the mouth to food. Use a clean utensil for each taste.

questions.prompt: A server is setting a table with clean forks. How should the forks be handled?
choices: Grip the tines with bare fingers
Carry them in the pocket of a used apron
Rest the food-contact ends on a dirty tray
questions.explanation: Holding handles protects the parts that will contact a customer's food and mouth.

questions.prompt: A guest returns to a self-service buffet for more food. Which practice should staff encourage?
choices: Use a clean plate for the next trip
Reuse the plate that still contains food scraps
Place a used fork in a communal serving pan
Mix leftovers from the plate into the buffet pan
questions.explanation: A used plate can contaminate serving utensils and shared food. A clean plate reduces that risk.

questions.prompt: A guest leaves half of a sandwich on a plate. May it be given to another guest?
choices: No, it has already been served and exposed to the first guest
Yes, if the remaining half looks untouched
Yes, if the guest says it tastes good
Yes, if the next guest receives a discount
questions.explanation: Returned food may have been contaminated. It must not be served to another customer.

questions.prompt: A container of sugar has a scoop stored inside it. Which placement best protects the sugar?
choices: Keep the handle above the sugar and out of contact with it
Bury the handle in the sugar
Use a drinking glass instead of a scoop
Leave the handle on the floor between uses
questions.explanation: Hands touch the handle, so keeping it clear of the food helps prevent contamination.

questions.prompt: A food handler washes hands correctly and then dries them on a soiled apron. What went wrong?
choices: The dirty apron can contaminate the clean hands again
Apron fabric automatically sanitizes the hands
Dry hands can no longer carry microorganisms
questions.explanation: Drying is part of hygienic handwashing. Use a suitable clean drying method rather than contaminated clothing.

questions.prompt: A food employee is ill with norovirus. Which statement about a small amount of contamination is correct?
choices: Even a very small amount of virus can contaminate food and make people sick
Food is safe whenever contamination is too small to see
Only visibly dirty food can spread the virus
questions.explanation: Norovirus can spread from very small amounts of contamination. Visual inspection cannot establish that food is safe.

questions.prompt: Someone vomits beside an exposed food preparation area. What should the food handler do first?
choices: Notify the person in charge and keep people and food away while the cleanup procedure is followed
Continue preparation and spray a normal air freshener
Wipe the area with the same cloth used on dining tables
Move the visible material without addressing nearby surfaces
questions.explanation: Vomiting can spread contamination to nearby surfaces and food. Follow the operation's specific cleanup and disinfection procedure.

questions.prompt: A sanitizer has been sprayed on a cutting board that still has grease and food pieces on it. What must happen?
choices: Clean and rinse the board before applying the sanitizer correctly
Assume the sanitizer removes every food particle
Add flour to absorb the grease and begin cutting
Use a dry towel without washing the board
questions.explanation: Sanitizing follows cleaning and rinsing. Remaining soil can prevent the sanitizer from reaching the surface effectively.

questions.prompt: A refrigerator contains ready-to-eat TCS food covered by a seven-day date-marking rule at 41 degrees F or below. It was prepared on Monday, counted as day one. What is day seven?
questions.explanation: Count the preparation day as the first day: Monday through Sunday is seven days. Follow any earlier product or local limit.

questions.prompt: A food handler combines two refrigerated, date-marked batches of the same ready-to-eat TCS food. Which date governs the combined batch?
choices: The earliest applicable discard date from either batch
Seven days after mixing, regardless of either original date
No date because combining food resets its age
questions.explanation: Combining food does not reset the older ingredient's storage time. Keep the earliest applicable discard date.

questions.prompt: A prep station has an accessible handwashing sink. Where should a food handler wash hands?
choices: In a bowl used to rinse raw chicken
In the sanitizer compartment of a utensil sink
In a mop bucket containing warm water
questions.explanation: A designated handwashing sink supports proper hand hygiene and keeps that activity separate from food and equipment washing.

questions.prompt: Which condition of a delivery of raw shell eggs requires attention before acceptance?
choices: Some shells are cracked and leaking
The outer case identifies the supplier
The case is carried on a clean trolley
The eggs arrive in protective packaging
questions.explanation: Cracked and leaking shells compromise the product's protection. Reject affected eggs and notify the person responsible for receiving.

questions.prompt: A worker sees a chemical spray bottle without a label. What should happen before anyone uses it?
choices: Identify and label it correctly under the operation's chemical procedures
Assume it is water because the liquid is clear
Taste a drop to identify it
Spray it on a food-contact surface to test its smell
questions.explanation: An unidentified chemical must not be guessed at. Correct identification and labeling help prevent misuse and contamination.

questions.prompt: A sealed carton of food is included in a supplier's recall notice. It looks normal. What should a food handler do?
choices: Separate the affected product, tell the manager and follow the recall directions
Serve it while waiting for a customer complaint
Remove the carton label and repackage it
Mix it with unaffected stock to dilute the risk
questions.explanation: Recall instructions apply even when food appears normal. Segregating affected stock prevents accidental service.

questions.prompt: A raw beef patty has just been thawed in a microwave. What should happen next?
choices: Cook it immediately using the required cooking procedure
Leave it on a prep counter until the evening shift
Treat it as ready-to-eat because microwave thawing sterilizes it
Hold it without temperature control until it feels cool
questions.explanation: Microwave thawing can leave parts of a food warm. Immediate cooking is required after thawing by this method.

questions.prompt: A busy kitchen has no safe way to wash hands because the water supply has stopped. What should a food handler do?
choices: Tell the person in charge immediately so safe operations can be assessed
Replace every handwashing step with a dry towel
Continue handling exposed food without telling anyone
Use drinking straws to apply sanitizer to the hands
questions.explanation: Loss of water can make essential hygiene impossible. The person in charge must address the problem before unsafe work continues.

questions.prompt: A handwashing sink runs out of soap during service. Which response is appropriate?
choices: Report the shortage and replenish soap before the next handwashing
Use the sink without soap for the rest of the shift
Wash hands in the food sanitizer solution
Borrow soap only after the restaurant closes
questions.explanation: Soap is needed for proper handwashing. Supplies must remain available throughout service.

questions.prompt: A delivery contains bags of flour with gnawed holes and loose powder beneath them. What should the food handler do?
choices: Reject the affected bags and inform the person in charge
Tape the holes and use the flour immediately
Sift the flour to remove all possible hazards
Mix the flour into an unopened bag
questions.explanation: Gnawed packaging indicates possible pest contamination. Taping or sifting does not establish that the product is safe.

questions.prompt: A pan of cooked rice is placed in a hot-holding unit that is still switched off. What must the food handler check?
choices: That the unit is operating correctly and the food remains at the required holding temperature
Only that the lid matches the pan
Whether the pan looks full enough for service
Whether the rice has a pleasant smell
questions.explanation: Hot-holding equipment must maintain the required food temperature. A suitable pan or normal smell does not prove safe holding.
